shortTheory.question: Define like and unlike parallel forces.
shortTheory.answer: If the parallel forces are acting in the same direction, then they are called like parallel forces and if their directions are opposite to one another, they are called unlike parallel forces.

shortTheory.question: What are rectangular components of a vector and their values?
shortTheory.answer: Usually, a force is resolved into two components which are perpendicular to each other. These are called its perpendicular or rectangular components of the force. The x-component of force F is denoted as F_x and y-component as F_y. F_x = F cos θ; F_y = F sin θ.

shortTheory.question: What is the line of action of a force?
shortTheory.answer: The line along which the force acts is called the line of action of the force.

shortTheory.question: Give an example of the body which is moving yet in equilibrium.
shortTheory.answer: A good example of dynamic equilibrium is a paratrooper. In a few second after the free fall, the parachute opens and a little later, the paratrooper starts descending with a uniform velocity. In this state, the force of gravity acting vertically downward on the paratrooper is balanced by the resistance of air on the parachute acting upward.

shortTheory.question: Why an accelerated body cannot be considered in equilibrium?
shortTheory.answer: A body is said to be in equilibrium if it has no acceleration. If a body is accelerated, it has acceleration and therefore cannot be in equilibrium.

definitions.text: All those forces which act parallel to one another are known as parallel forces.
If the parallel forces are acting in the same direction, then they are called like parallel forces and if their directions are opposite to one another, they are called unlike parallel forces.
A force which is equal to the sum of all the forces is known as resultant force.
As forces are vectors, so forces can also be added by head-to-tail rule.
If the distance between two points of the body remains the same under the action of a force, it is called a rigid body.

definitions.term: Line of action of a force
definitions.text: The line along which the force acts is called the line of action of the force.
The perpendicular distance of the line of action of a force from the axis of rotation is known as moment arm of the force or simply moment arm.
Moment of a force or torque is defined as the product of the force and the moment arm.
When two equal and opposite parallel forces act at two different points of the same body, they form a couple.
A component of a vector is its effective value in a given direction.
When a body is in balanced position, the sum of clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about that point.
Centre of gravity is that point where total weight of the body appears to be acting.
The centre of mass of a body is that point where the whole mass of the body is assumed to be concentrated.
A body is said to be in equilibrium if it has no acceleration.
A body at rest is in static equilibrium whereas a body moving with uniform velocity is in dynamic equilibrium.
A body is said to be in translational equilibrium only if the vector sum of all the external forces acting on it is equal to zero.

definitions.term: First condition of equilibrium in components
definitions.text: The sum of all the components of forces along x-axis should be zero and the sum of all the components of forces along y-axis should also be zero.
The vector sum of all the torques acting on a body about any point must be zero.
A body is said to be in a state of stable equilibrium, if after a slight tilt, it comes back to its original position.
A body is said to be in a state of unstable equilibrium, if after a slight tilt, it tends to move on further away from its original position.
A body is in neutral equilibrium, if it comes to rest in its new position after disturbance without any change in its centre of mass.

definitions.term: Determining the centre of gravity of an irregular plane lamina
definitions.text: Each time the object is suspended, its centre of gravity lies on the vertical line drawn from the point of suspension with the help of a plumb line. The exact position of the centre of gravity is at the point where two such lines cross each other as shown in Fig 4.15(b).

Therefore, we are justified to predict that analogous to Newton's first law of motion, a rotating object will continue to do so with constant angular velocity unless acted upon by a resultant moment (torque).
The force that causes an object to move in a circle at constant speed is called the centripetal force.

fullMarks: For a definition or law, write the complete statement clearly before explaining or applying it.
For moments, identify the pivot, perpendicular distance, and clockwise or anticlockwise direction; use N m for each moment.
For equilibrium questions, show both force conditions, ΣF_x = 0 and ΣF_y = 0, and include Στ = 0 when rotational balance is relevant.
For a numerical, write the given values in SI units first, then the formula, substitution with units, and final answer with its unit and sensible significant figures.
For force components, state whether the angle is measured from the horizontal; use F_x = F cos θ and F_y = F sin θ for that angle.
For a principle-of-moments question, write total clockwise moments = total anticlockwise moments and show each force × perpendicular distance.
For questions about finding a lamina’s centre of gravity, describe suspending it from two points, drawing each vertical with a plumb line, and marking their intersection; label the diagram.
For equilibrium and stability diagrams, label the weight, reaction or tension, centre of gravity, pivot or base, and relevant force directions.

mistakes: Using F sin θ for the horizontal component when θ is measured from the horizontal; fix: F_x = F cos θ and F_y = F sin θ for that angle.
Using the distance along a sloping force as the moment arm; fix: use the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force’s line of action.
Forgetting to convert centimetres to metres before calculating torque; fix: convert the moment arm to m so the answer is in N m.
Adding clockwise and anticlockwise moments with the same sign; fix: choose a sign convention or set total clockwise moments equal to total anticlockwise moments.
Checking only that the resultant force is zero and forgetting rotational balance; fix: also check that Στ = 0 for complete equilibrium.
Treating a moving body as automatically out of equilibrium; fix: a body moving with uniform velocity has no acceleration and can be in dynamic equilibrium.
Writing a centripetal-force answer with radius in the numerator or forgetting to square speed; fix: use F_c = mv² ÷ r and substitute SI values.
